_about: Question sheets for tool management (MCP-22). Read by plan_tool_call (MCP-23, not built yet) with tool_notes.json. One sheet per request family: what the user asks for, not how the tool works. Each row: kind (deciding = picks the tool; required = the result fails if it is wrong), ask (plain words for the user), read_from (how to answer it from the user's words or files first), answers (what each answer means for the tool and settings), default (used on 'your call' or when the user does not answer), why (the tool note and benchmark cases behind it). A row is asked only when it applies and the user's words and files do not answer it. Drafted 2026-11-13; not yet confirmed by the user.
rules: Answer every row from the user's words and attached files first. Ask only the deciding and required rows that are still open.

Ask as few questions as possible: only those whose answer would change the result and that the user's words and files do not answer. Ask them all together in one message, once, in plain words, each with what happens if the user skips it. Never ask a second round: anything still open after the user answers takes its default.
'Your call', 'you pick', or no answer: use the row's default and tell the user what was chosen.

Keep every concrete detail the user gave (counts, colours, materials, names, exact words) in the tool's prompt word for word. A01a: 'matte black on marble' became a silver bottle on white when the details were dropped.
Free-tier models only (tool_notes.json, free_models). Never name a paid model.
Keep the user's media unless the user asked for it to be redrawn or re-made.
When no tool does the job (a GAP row), say so plainly and offer the nearest real option. Do not send the user's media through a tool that redraws it instead.
A request for a film of several shots or scenes goes to video composition (plan_request), not to these sheets.

new_picture.is: A new picture from words: a product shot, an illustration, a post, a flyer, a logo, a thumbnail, a meme.

generate_image.style.tool: ai-illustration-generator for an illustration, else none; never ai-photo-generator or movie-poster-generator

rows.ask: What should it look like: the colour and material of the subject, the setting or background, and the light?
read_from: Colours, materials, finishes ('matte black', 'amber glass', 'white leather').
A setting or surface ('on marble', 'on a café table', 'plain white background').
Light or mood ('soft light', 'premium', 'warm').
Only the subject named ('a water bottle') → open: ask.

answers.any: Put every detail in the prompt word for word.

rows.default: A clean product look: the subject centred on a plain light background, soft light.
rows.why: A01a: the user had 'matte black on marble' in mind; without the question the bottle came out steel on grey (2). With the planner asking: 4, 4, 4. generate_image limit: a vague user's details get lost (A01a).

rows.ask: Should the picture have any words on it? If so, what exactly should they say?
read_from: Text in quotes, or after 'headline', 'saying', 'text:', 'title'.
A brand or shop name the user spelled out.
'No text', 'no words' → none.

answers.none: generate_image; say 'no text' in the prompt.
answers.exact words: generate_image with no words in the prompt, then add_words_to_media with the exact words (MCP-25).

rows.why: generate_image antitype: headlines misspelt or changed (A02b 'CEAN UP YOUR BACH', A02c, A06b). Test wlive1: A02a 4 with the chain.

rows.ask: What shape: square, wide (16:9), tall (9:16, for stories), or 4:5 (for a feed post)?
read_from: 'Story', 'reel', 'TikTok', 'vertical', 'tall' → 9:16.
'YouTube thumbnail', 'banner', 'wide', 'landscape' → 16:9.
'Instagram post', 'square', 'logo' → 1:1.
'4:5', 'portrait post' → 4:5.

answers.4:5: generate_image 1:1, then edit_image (qwen-image-2.1, aspect_ratio 4:5); reframe_media has no 4:5 (MCP-34).

rows.why: generate_image limit: aspect setting is 1:1, 16:9, 9:16 only. A03 4:5 flyers made by edit_image with qwen: 3.6.

rows.ask: One size, or the same design in several sizes?
read_from: 'In three sizes', '1:1, 9:16 and 16:9', 'for feed and stories'.

answers.several: Make one, then reframe_media for each other shape, then add_words_to_media on each (MCP-26).

rows.why: G36a/b asked for matching sizes; separate generations do not match.

rows.ask: Do you need a transparent background (to put the picture on other things)?
read_from: 'Transparent', 'PNG with no background', 'cut out'.

answers.yes: generate_image with no words, remove_image_background, then add_words_to_media.

rows.why: remove_image_background antitype: thin letters fade or smear (A06c 2.7).

rows.ask: A meme with your own picture and your own words, or a known meme template with a joke on your topic?
read_from: An attached picture, or top and bottom text given → own.
'Make a meme about X' with no picture or text → template.

answers.own: add_words_to_media on the picture (top and bottom).

rows.default: Template when no picture is attached, else own.
rows.why: create_meme antitype: it uses its templates and writes its own caption, which can drift off the topic (G39b).

change_picture.is: A change to the user's own picture: a new shape, words on it, an edit, bigger, a cut-out.

rows.ask: Should I keep your picture exactly and only reshape it or add words, or redraw it with a change?
read_from: 'Square', 'vertical', 'fit', 'crop', 'resize', 'add a caption', 'put text on' → keep.
'Change X to Y', 'remove', 'replace', 'make it look like', 'put it on a new background' → redraw.

answers.keep: Image by code: reframe_media for the shape, add_words_to_media for words.

rows.why: edit_image antitype: a new shape came back 640x384 (B12a-d: 1.0 to 1.3); words misspelt (B11a). Test wlive1: B12a 1 → 4, B11a 2 → 4 with the code tools.

rows.ask: To fit the new shape, may I cut the edges, or should I keep the whole picture with bars or a blurred copy around it?
read_from: 'Keep the whole', 'don't crop', 'don't cut off' → pad or fill.
'Plain padding', 'bars', 'match the background' → pad, colour of the background.
'Blurred copy' → fill.
'Crop', 'zoom in', 'fill the frame' → crop.

answers.crop: reframe_media how=crop, focus on the subject.
answers.bars: reframe_media how=pad, color from the user or the picture's background.

rows.why: reframe_media type and limits (B12a fill 4, B12d pad 3).

rows.ask: Where in the picture is the part that must stay in?
read_from: Look at the attached picture (Read).
'The shoe is on the left' → focus 0.
rows.why: B12d: 'don't just crop the middle'.

rows.ask: What exactly should it say, and where: top, middle, bottom or a corner?
read_from: Quoted text.
'Near the bottom', 'at the top', 'in the corner'.

answers.any: add_words_to_media with text, place, size, style.

rows.default: Place bottom, size large, style shadow.
rows.why: add_words_to_media (B11a 4, E29c 4 in wlive1).

rows.ask: Should the words look printed on something in the scene (a sign, a label), or sit on top of the photo like a caption?
read_from: 'Chalkboard saying', 'a sign that reads', 'on the label' → on an object.
'Caption', 'over the photo', 'text on top' → on top.

answers.on an object: edit_image to add the object with the words; tell the user the letters may be misspelt.

rows.why: add_words_to_media antitype: drawn words do not follow an object (B11b).

rows.ask: Only bigger, or also cleaned up (scratches, blur)? Cleaning up can change faces slightly.
read_from: 'Upscale', 'bigger', 'higher resolution' → bigger.
'Restore', 'clean up', 'old photo', 'scratches', 'blurry' → also fixed.

answers.fixed: upscale_image, scale 2, and tell the user faces may be redrawn slightly.

rows.why: upscale_image antitype and limits: faces regenerated (B13a 2.0); preserve 3 in wlive1, faces still smoothed. Mode undecided: preserve scored 2 and balanced 3 on B13a (one run each).

rows.applies: a colour change of the whole picture
rows.ask: Which colour change: warmer, cooler, black and white, brighter, or more contrast? And how strong: a little or a lot?
read_from: 'Warmer', 'cosier', 'golden' → warmer.
'Cooler', 'colder', 'blue tint' → cooler.
'Black and white', 'grayscale', 'remove the colour' → black and white.
'Brighter', 'lighter' → brighter; 'punchier', 'more contrast' → contrast.
rows.why: MCP-35, adjust_colours (2026-11-14): changes only the colours, nothing redrawn. Before: edit_image redrew the picture (B07c, J49a). Not benchmarked yet.

rows.applies: two or more pictures in one (side by side, before and after, a collage)
rows.ask: Keep each photo exactly as it is, side by side (or in a grid), or redraw them into one new picture?
read_from: 'Side by side', 'before and after', 'keep both photos as they are' → side by side.
'Show how it could look', 'make a combined picture' → redraw.

answers.side by side: put_pictures_side_by_side with layout, aspect and labels (e.g. ['Before', 'After']); the photos are kept whole.
answers.redraw: edit_image (qwen-image-2.1) with both pictures; tell the user the photos will be redrawn.

rows.why: MCP-30, put_pictures_side_by_side (2026-11-14). Before: edit_image redrew and cropped both photos (G35a 2.0, G35b 1.7). Not benchmarked yet.

faces.is: A face or head from one picture onto a person in a photo or video, or a headshot from a photo.

swap_face_in_photo.face_swap_mode: individual-faces only when several people each get their own face

rows.ask: (Not asked: a rule.) A real public figure without consent, a child's face, or a fake endorsement: refuse and say why.
read_from: A celebrity's name, 'without permission', a child's photo.

answers.none: Go ahead: an adult's own face, or a person who agreed.
answers.any of these: Refuse plainly. Offer an invented or illustrated person instead (for a child: a generic illustrated child). Do not ask for another photo of the person.

rows.why: C14c, J54a, J54b. w24on J54b: declined, but kept asking for the boy's photo and offered no illustrated alternative.

rows.ask: (Read from the files.) Is the target a photo or a video?
read_from: The attached files.

answers.video: swap_face_in_video; tell the user the face may only look similar and no head swap exists for video.

rows.why: User, 2026-11-13: head swap for faces. Test: C14b 1.5 → 4; C14a head swap clearly the person, face swap a blend. swap_face_in_video limit (C15a 2.7).

rows.applies: more than one person in the target
rows.ask: There are several people in the picture. Which one gets the new face?
read_from: 'The woman on the right', 'the pilot', 'the one in blue'.
Look at the picture (Read).

answers.one person: swap_head_in_photo; if it changes the wrong person, detect_faces then swap_face_in_photo individual-faces.
answers.each a different face: detect_faces, then swap_face_in_photo or swap_face_in_video individual-faces.

rows.why: C14b: asked which person, then head swap: 4.

rows.ask: The whole clip, or only part of it? If part, from when to when?
read_from: 'The first 5 seconds', 'from 0:10 to 0:20'.
rows.why: swap_face_in_video antitype: asked for 5 s, delivered all 10 s (C15a).

rows.ask: Any shape or background you need (for example square, plain grey)?
read_from: 'Square', 'LinkedIn', 'plain grey background', 'navy blazer'.

answers.set shape or background: edit_image (qwen-image-2.1) with the shape and background in the prompt; reframe_media 1:1 if needed.

rows.why: generate_headshot antitype: 928x1152 and an office background for 'square, plain grey' (A05a 3.0). Test wlive1: A05a 5 with edit_image.

change_video.is: A change to the user's own video: a new shape, a cut, words or a watermark, subtitles, a new ending, music or a voice over it.

rows.ask: Should I keep your footage exactly and only cut it, reshape it or add text, or re-make the whole video in a new look?
read_from: 'Vertical', 'square', 'trim', 'cut', 'shorter', 'add a watermark', 'add subtitles' → keep.
'Make it look like anime', 'restyle', 'change the scene' → re-make.

answers.keep: Video by code (reframe_media, trim_media, add_words_to_media) or add_subtitles_to_video.
answers.re-make: edit_video; tell the user nothing of the original is kept.

rows.why: edit_video antitype: never the right tool in 36 runs (1.7). Test wlive1: E25a 1 → 4, E29c 1 → 4, J49c 2.5 → 5 with the code tools.

rows.ask: Who or what must stay in the frame? May I cut the sides, or should I keep the whole picture with bars?
read_from: 'Keep her centred' → crop, focus on her.
'Two people talking', 'show whoever is speaking' → follow the speaker.
'Keep the whole picture', 'with bars', 'padding' → pad.

answers.one subject: reframe_media crop with focus on the subject (get_last_frame to see where).
answers.follow the speaker: trim_media at each change of speaker, reframe_media each part with its own focus, join_videos (MCP-27).

rows.default: Crop on the middle; pad when the user says keep everything.
rows.why: reframe_media (E25a 4 in wlive1); E25b two speakers.

rows.ask: Which part should I keep: from when to when? I can't watch the clip, so if you want 'the best part', tell me roughly where it is.
read_from: 'The first 5 seconds', 'from 0:12 to 0:20', 'cut the end'.
'The best 10 seconds', 'the boring parts' → ask where.
rows.default: From the start, the length asked; say the part was picked without watching.
rows.why: trim_media limit: 'the best part' picked blind (E26b 3 in wlive1; MCP-07).

rows.applies: change only part of a clip
rows.ask: Keep the start as it is and make a new ending from where it stops?
read_from: 'Change only the ending', 'keep the first five seconds'.

answers.yes: trim_media the start, get_last_frame, create_video_from_image for the new part, join_videos (MCP-27).

rows.default: Yes when the user says 'only the ending'.
rows.why: J50b.

rows.ask: What exactly should it say, where, and for the whole clip or only part of it?
read_from: Quoted text; 'bottom right', 'corner'; 'watermark', 'subtle', 'see-through'.

answers.watermark: add_words_to_media: corner, size small, style shadow, opacity 0.6.

rows.why: E29c 1 → 4 in wlive1 with the watermark settings.

rows.ask: Subtitles in the language that is spoken, or translated into another language?
read_from: 'Spanish subtitles' on an English clip → translated.
'Subtitles', 'captions' alone → spoken language.

answers.translated: GAP (MCP-33): tell the user; translate_video changes the voice, not only the subtitles.

rows.why: add_subtitles_to_video antitype (E24b 2.0); best_settings highlight (weak).

rows.ask: (Not asked.) If the clip has no speech, say so and make nothing.
read_from: The user says it may be silent; the subtitle job fails.
rows.why: add_subtitles_to_video antitype (E24c).

rows.applies: music or a voice-over on the user's video
rows.ask: Should your video's own sound stay clear with the music under it, be lowered, or be replaced by the new sound?
read_from: 'Keep my voice', 'under the radio calls', 'keep the conversation' → keep.
'Replace the sound', 'instead of the conversation', 'new soundtrack' → replace.
'Add some music' alone → under.

answers.keep: Make the sound (generate_music, or the voice generator), then add_sound_to_video original=keep.
answers.under: Make the sound, then add_sound_to_video original=under.
answers.replace: Make the sound, then add_sound_to_video original=replace.

rows.default: keep when the video has speech, else under.
rows.why: MCP-29, add_sound_to_video (2026-11-13): E27a-c 2.0 and E28a-c 1.3 to 2.0 had no tool. Not benchmarked yet.

rows.applies: a logo or picture on the video, or a card before or after it
rows.ask: Where should the logo go (which corner), how big, and for the whole clip? (For a card: what words, what colour, how long, before or after the clip?)
read_from: 'In the top-right corner', 'small', 'throughout' → place, size, whole clip.
'End card', '2-second black card with white text' → card: words, colour, seconds, after.

answers.logo: remove_image_background first if the logo has a background, then put_picture_on_video (place, size 0.15, opacity).
answers.card: make_card_clip with the words, background, seconds, like_video = the user's clip and attach=after (an end card) or before (a title card): one file, the clip's sound kept.

rows.default: Logo: top_right, size 0.15, the whole clip. Card: 2 s, black, white words, after the clip.
rows.why: MCP-31 put_picture_on_video, MCP-32 make_card_clip (2026-11-14). Before: no tool (E29a 1.3, E29b 2.0). Not benchmarked yet. Run wnew E29b: join_videos failed (media_tools.join calls ffmpeg by name), so the card tool attaches the card itself.

new_video.is: One new clip from words or from a picture. Several shots or scenes go to video composition.

rows.ask: (Read from the files.) Start from your picture, or from words only?
read_from: An attached picture → from the picture.

answers.picture: create_video_from_image; it keeps the picture's shape, so reframe_media after if another shape was asked.

rows.why: create_video_from_image limit: no shape setting.

rows.ask: How long, in seconds?
read_from: '8-second', 'a short clip' (ask), '10 s'.
rows.why: plan_request asked 'a short clip' as 8 s when the user wanted 6 s (2026-11-05 benchmark).

rows.ask: Wide (16:9), tall (9:16) or square?
read_from: 'Widescreen', 'vertical', 'TikTok', 'square'.

answers.any: aspect_ratio (text to video); reframe_media after (picture to video).

rows.why: J51a 9:16 asked, 16:9 delivered.

rows.ask: With sound, or silent?
read_from: 'Silent', 'no sound', 'with music'.
rows.why: D23b: sound came back when silence was asked.

rows.ask: Any words that must appear on screen, spelled exactly?
read_from: Quoted text, 'with the title', 'label'.

answers.exact words: Make the clip without words, then add_words_to_media (MCP-25).

rows.why: create_video_from_text antitype: labels missing (I46b).

talking.is: A person in a photo or video speaks given words.

rows.ask: (Read from the files.) Is there a person on screen who should say the words?
read_from: A photo of a person → talking photo.
A video of a presenter → lip sync.
No person → a voice-over (GAP on the user's video).

answers.video with a presenter: create_lip_sync_video; tell the user the footage may be re-made.
answers.no presenter: Voice-over on the video: make the voice, then add_sound_to_video (change_video sound_on_video).

rows.why: Ray's finding: narration with a presenter uses lip sync, without one the voice cloner. create_lip_sync_video antitype (E28a, E28c).

rows.ask: What exactly should they say? Or shall I write it?
read_from: Quoted line; 'say exactly'.
'You write it' → write it, with no invented facts (prices, dates).
rows.default: Write a short line from the request, no invented facts.
rows.why: C17a, C17b.

rows.ask: (Not asked.) Set the length from the line: about 2.5 words a second, plus half a second.
read_from: The line.

answers.—: end_seconds from the line; if the user asked a longer clip, say the end will be silent, or trim_media after.

rows.why: create_talking_photo limit: 8 s clip, 4.5 s of speech, 3 s silent (wlive2 C17a).

rows.ask: Square, tall or wide?
read_from: 'Square video', 'for stories'.

answers.any: reframe_media after: create_talking_photo keeps the photo's shape.

rows.why: create_talking_photo antitype: 1024x1536 for 'square' (C17a/b).

sound.is: Music or voice as a sound file: a music bed, a voice-over, a podcast intro, a dialogue.

rows.ask: (Read from the files.) A sound file on its own, or on your video?
read_from: An attached video and 'add music to this' → on the video.

answers.on the video: Make the sound, then add_sound_to_video (change_video sound_on_video).

rows.why: E27a-c.

rows.ask: How long, in seconds?
read_from: '10-second', 'a 20-second intro'.

answers.under 15 s: generate_music 15 s, then trim_media or mix_audio to the length, with a short fade-out (MCP-28).

rows.why: generate_music antitype: API minimum 15 s (F30a). Test wlive1: F30a 2.5 → 4 with the cut.

rows.ask: What mood or style? With or without vocals?
read_from: 'Lo-fi', 'warm', 'tense', 'upbeat'; 'no vocals', 'instrumental'.

answers.any: style prompt; instrumental when no vocals.

rows.why: F30b/c 4.0 with the tool's own choice.

rows.ask: One voice or several? Over music or on its own?
read_from: 'Two hosts', 'two voices', 'A says, B says'; 'with music behind'.

answers.several voices: The voice generator per line, then join_videos (sound files).
answers.over music: Then mix_audio: music first, voice from a few seconds in, music at about 0.25.

rows.why: F31b, F32a, F32b (MCP-28). The voice generator is hidden upstream (MCP-11).
